name: Grave
identity: Turn lost cards into Corpse tokens and Remnant. Haunt enemy cards to force a choice, or reserve Remnant for recovery and Death Anchor.
loop: Create Corpse records when your cards are lost → spend them for Remnant → Haunt visible enemy cards → use Remnant for recovery, or reserve it for Death Anchor.
statuses: When damage or a sacrifice permanently removes one of your cards, you may place a Corpse token beside that card. Create no more than two Corpses each round. If full, discard an old Corpse token before making a new one. Spending a Corpse does not bring back its card. If the card is recovered, remove its Corpse token.

During Offensive, spend 1 Corpse to gain 2 Remnant. Use this once per round. During Offensive, you may also spend 2 Remnant to place Haunt on an enemy card in their discard pile, once per round. Remnant pays for other Grave cards and abilities. Keep unused Remnant.
Negative card mark · enemy card · max 2 per player

Mark an enemy card in their discard pile or a card revealed because damage may remove it. When they play the marked card, they must pay 1 extra Energy or take 1 status damage after using it. Then erase Haunt. If damage removes the marked card instead, erase Haunt and give the player who placed it 1 Remnant. Only your first Haunt used each round can charge extra Energy, deal damage or give Remnant. Later marked cards simply lose their Haunt when played or removed that round. Erase unused Haunts at the end of the following round.

When damage would leave you with no health cards, you may spend Death Anchor and 2 Remnant to recover one of your cards lost to damage earlier in the battle. Put it in your discard pile before defeat is decided. This saves you only once per battle. It cannot recover a sacrifice or work without a card lost to earlier damage. You must also have one of your two recovery uses left this round.

pairs: Sacrifice earns Ichor once per round and can create a Corpse for Remnant. The sacrificed card stays removed; Grave’s recovery must choose a different card previously lost to damage.
Losing an Ember-marked card to damage can give Heat and a Corpse. Haunt can also earn Heat if the enemy chooses its status damage instead of paying the extra Energy.
Regrowth can recover a card with a Corpse token, removing that token. Spend the Corpse for Remnant before recovering its card to get use from both effects, while paying each recovery cost normally.
Grave can recover a lost card into discard; Beacon selects that card for the next Income draw. Recovering the card removes its Corpse token. Only Death Anchor provides a last-chance rescue.
example: Damage removes an Ember-marked card: Flame gains Heat and Grave may create a Corpse beside that card. Spend the Corpse for Remnant. If you later recover the card, it no longer has a Corpse to spend. A sacrificed card can create a Corpse but cannot be recovered.
counter: An enemy may pay Haunt’s extra Energy to avoid its damage. Pressure Remnant spending so Death Anchor lacks its two-stack cost. A Corpse token is not a health card and cannot save a defeated creature by itself.
balance: Corpse creates no more than two tokens per round and keeps no more than three. A recovered card loses its token. Haunt can charge, damage or reward only once per round for the player who placed it. Death Anchor is Grave’s one last-chance rescue per battle and still shares the normal recovery limit.

Corpse.job: Remember a lost card so its remains can be spent.
Corpse.example: Sacrifice a card and mark it with a Corpse. Spend the Corpse for Remnant later; the sacrificed card stays removed.

Remnant.job: Turn lost cards into hauntings and recovery tools.
Remnant.example: Spend a Corpse for two Remnant, then spend those Remnant to Haunt a discarded enemy card.

Haunt.job: Make one card costly to use, or useful to you when lost.
Haunt.example: The enemy plays a Haunted card with no spare Energy. The card still works, but they take 1 damage afterward.

Death Anchor.job: Offer Grave one costly last chance to survive.
Death Anchor.example: The current hit removes your last card. Spend the Anchor and Remnant to recover a card lost on a previous hit and stay alive with one health card.
